I dunno if this is due to my data or a simple bug in survival packages

all of you this strange case for usefull tips.

Thanks in advance,

Best wishes

messages.body_plain:
On 5 February 2010 10:47, David Winsemius <dwins...@comcast.net> wrote:
> On Feb 4, 2010, at 2:16 PM, danielem wrote:

>> Dears RattleRs,
>>
>> fitting a survival model with cox, I obtain scores with values bigger
>> than 1.x, eg. 1.023....
>
> What do you mean by "scores"?

I think "score" means you apply a model to a dataset with the Score
option of the Evaluate tab. This uses the predict function
(predict.coxph) underneath.

The default "predict" in Rattle  is with type="risk". Interpret the
risk as relative to 1. So a risk score above 1 is a higher risk than
the average in the population and below 1 is a lower risk than the
average in the population.

Regards,
Graham

messages.subject: trouble installing Rattle on Vista
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I hope you can help.  The first time I installed I just typed,

> library(rattle)
> rattle()

in R.  I did not follow the special instructions for installing on MS Windows.  I am using Vista, 32 bit.  The Rattle data tab has no CSV option and I cannot locate the audit data set.  When I select <Execute> it asks if I want to load the weather data, but again, no reference to audit data.  I've tried uninstalling R and then following the special instructions for Windows, but the result is the same.  When I type,
> install.packages("rattle", dependencies=c("Depends", "Suggests"))
very little happens, presumably because I went through the installation process once before.  Is the solution to completely wipe out all R and Rattle related programs and start fresh?  I know how to uninstall R, but how do I uninstall Rattle and all related programs?  Is there an easier solution?

The version of R I installed is 2.10.1
The version of Rattle is 2.5.21

Thanks for your answer.

The current version of Rattle uses the weather dataset by default. The CSV option has been replaced by Spreadsheet, and you can identify a .csv file.  Rattle does undergo regular development and so some of these things do change over time, and so some older papers will be slightly different.

For the public record: we resolved the issue offline.

The problem was that the baskets contained repeated items. If we
remove the repeated items it works.

I'll capture this error in Rattle so that it will pop up a message
when this happens and provide the suggestion to remove the repeated
items.

Thanks to Ross for reporting the problem and helping resolve it.

Regards,
Graham

messages.subject: Re: error in reading CSV file
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jüri,

This is probably an issue with locale. A work around might be:

> ds <- read.csv(system.file("csv", "weather.csv", package="rattle"))

That might load the dataset without trying to use UTF-8 encoding.

Then in Rattle on the Data tab choose the R Dataset option and under
the Data Name drop down box choose "ds", then Execute

Let me know how you go.

Regards,
Graham
